question: For this Codex lane-release replacement, is focused runner/Codex regression proof enough after the dirty branch is refreshed, or do maintainers require live wedged app-server/channel proof before merge?
rationale: The code path and regression support the fix, but the PR changes lane ownership while a plugin-owned transport may still be cleaning up and the linked incident is user-visible message loss.

options.title: Accept Focused Proof After Clean Rebase
options.body: Refresh the dirty head, preserve current-main abort semantics, rerun required checks, and accept the focused regression as sufficient for this runner-owned contract.

options.title: Require Live Wedge Proof
options.body: Pause merge until a live or Crabbox Codex app-server wedge demonstrates that late cleanup does not corrupt session state or delivery.

options.title: Pause Or Close Replacement
options.body: Stop this replacement if maintainers prefer to redesign the lane-release boundary or roll it into a broader Codex recovery effort.

recommendation.title: Accept Focused Proof After Clean Rebase
recommendation.body: Refresh the dirty head, preserve current-main abort semantics, rerun required checks, and accept the focused regression as sufficient for this runner-owned contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the adjacent lane-release contract and triggered automerge handling on the superseded source PR, making them the strongest available routing owner for the proof/merge decision.
